ea30f6fb362c7dd3.text: Hi! I am Vidi, your guide for this lesson.

ba9005e318212307.text: We will learn Ohm's law on a real moving simulation, one small step at a time. Ask me anything, any time, in the box below.

a12ab14b7abbcca7.text: Watch the meter. The battery switches on, the push spreads through the wire, and the current climbs to a steady value.

a661f0085b29bfc3.text: Drag the Voltage slider to 5 volts or more. Watch the bright dot climb the straight line.

8d768b1ae9c434ad.text: Hint: The voltage V slider is on the right side of the simulation.

8b8a577bd3f463f8.text: Now push the voltage up by at least 3 more volts. The dot slides along the SAME straight line, that straight line is Ohm's law.

6117fbede41a1f3f.text: Raise the Resistance to 15 ohms or more. Watch the line get steeper, steeper means more resistance.

14abe4adb4bc2ffe.text: Hint: The resistance R slider is on the right side of the simulation.

820799a388abdf55.text: Watch the two counting meters, one before the resistor and one after it. The counts stay equal. Nothing is used up.

eade60b62b049349.text: This wire is a glowing filament bulb. Push the voltage to 10 volts and watch the line bend, the hot filament does not follow the straight line.

d6c811e1f595f062.text: You saw it! The battery gave the push, and the current climbed to a steady value. That push is called voltage.

c4ef511828640549.text: Nice work! You raised the voltage and the bright dot climbed the straight line. More push, more current.

8fbf70537f706574.text: Exactly! The dot stayed on the same straight line. That straight line through zero IS Ohm's law.

69c6eccee1599327.text: You did it! You raised the resistance and the line became steeper. A steeper line means more resistance.

c0ddb8dc3773ac20.text: Right! The count going in and the count coming out stayed equal the whole time. Current is never used up.

e0192a7281af2b46.text: You found the limit! The hot filament bends the line, its resistance rises as it heats. The straight line only holds at constant temperature.

601a3ae4b368cb0f.text: Watch this part again: PRIMARY aha, the swept voltage V, current I trace is a straight line through the origin

3e7d4b51e55f94a4.text: Watch this part again: resistance R equals voltage V /i, resistance is the slope; more resistance R tilts the line steeper

b61ac7045e9cde7b.text: Watch the two counting meters, the count going in and the count coming out stay equal the whole time.

1b3d025d46bbd8a5.text: Push the voltage high and watch the bright trace bend away from the straight reference line.

915129b3c3cf2643.text: Well done! You completed this step.

bbc97d74e39d05b1.text: The slider for this step could not be found. Watch the simulation, then press Continue.

f6f56d102a63dea5.text: Watch this part again. Ask me if anything is unclear.

f309e159e9c4c88f.text: Both sliders are yours now. Make the current large, then small. Watch the graph follow you, and ask me anything you wonder about.
